item.research_question: How does increasing the atomic size difference (δ) affect the microstructure stability, grain growth activation energy, and mechanical properties of single FCC phase high-entropy alloys?
item.processing_route: Arc melting at 500 A in 0.01 Torr vacuum, homogenization at 1100 °C for 6 h, water quenching or furnace cooling, cold rolling with 70% thickness reduction, and annealing between 900 °C and 1100 °C for various times followed by water quenching
item.test_conditions: Tensile testing at ambient temperature with a strain rate of 10⁻³ s⁻¹; grain growth analysis via annealing at 900–1100 °C for various durations
key_findings: The atomic size difference increased from 1.18% in CoCrFeMnNi to 2.77% in Al0.2CoCrFeMnNi and 3.65% in Al0.3CoCrCu0.3FeNi.
The activation energy of grain growth for Al0.2CoCrFeMnNi was calculated to be 434.4 kJ/mol.
The activation energy of grain growth for Al0.3CoCrCu0.3FeNi was the highest among the three alloys at 761.3 kJ/mol.
Al0.3CoCrCu0.3FeNi exhibited a yield strength of 500 MPa and ultimate tensile strength of 717 MPa after annealing at 900 °C for 5 h.
All three alloys maintained a single FCC phase structure after homogenization and cooling, showing good workability with 70% cold rolling reduction without cracks.

The grain size of Al0.3CoCrCu0.3FeNi after annealing at 1000 °C for 120 min was not explicitly stated as a single value in the text, but the activation energy calculation was based on grain sizes measured at different temperatures and times.
item.mechanism: The authors argue that a large atomic size difference causes high lattice distortion, which increases the energy level of the grain compared to an undistorted state. This creates a higher driving force requirement for recrystallization, leading to higher activation energy for grain growth. Additionally, solute atoms (particularly Al) act as obstacles that pin dislocations in stable lattice sites, increasing strength through solid solution hardening and the pinning effect.
item.limitations: The text states that 'the lattice distortion effect on properties of HEAs is yet an open question still await to be solved'.
quotes: The activation energy of grain growth is 761.3 kJ/mol.
The mechanical properties of Al0.3CoCrCu0.3FeNi are better than those of CoCrFeMnNi because of high lattice distortion and high solid solution hardening.
A large atomic size difference indicates that a high activation energy is needed for grain growth.
